chunks: And from him, from Fadalah, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"There is no prayer at midday except on Friday."
And from him, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskhan, from Ismail ibn al-Khaliq, who said:

"I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the time of Dhuhr prayer, and he said: 'After the sun has passed its zenith (Zawal) by a pace or thereabouts, except on Friday or during travel, for its time is when the sun passes its zenith.'

key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: solar zenith (when the sun begins to decline)

ai.seo_question: When does the Dhuhr prayer time begin on Friday compared to other days?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the temporal distinction between the general rule for Dhuhr prayer and the specific exception for Fridays and travel. While the standard onset is marked by a slight deviation from the zenith (zawal), Friday and journeying allow for immediate prayer at the exact moment of zenith, reflecting the accelerated or distinct spiritual status of these occasions in Shia jurisprudence.
